audit_findings.title: One-time FY2025 cash-tax acceleration may be embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $70.0m FY2025 cash-flow acceleration, equal to 21.5% of the $326.3m OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A transitional cash-tax benefit increases FY2025 operating cash flow and therefore the OE anchor propagated through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, OBBBA resulted in a decrease in our deferred tax assets of approximately $70 million, primarily due to the immediate expensing of domestic research and development expenditures and a corresponding increase in both operating and free cash flow.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates an approximately $70m FY2025 cash-flow benefit from eliminating previously capitalized domestic R&D tax balances. The record does not show that this transition benefit was normalized out of OE. Its size relative to the anchor makes it reasonably capable of materially changing all scenario values, even though ongoing immediate deductions on future R&D may remain recurring.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2025 cash taxes and deferred taxes through the OE bridge, separate the one-time release of prior capitalized R&D from recurring tax effects, and rerun all scenarios with normalized cash taxes.

audit_findings.title: Forecast reinvestment may lag the disclosed capital-spending ramp
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 capital expenditures were $191.6m and developed-software investment was $19.2m, while first-half 2026 amounts were $56.8m and $8.3m, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Insufficient deductions for necessary property, equipment, manufacturing capacity, software and other capitalized operating assets would overstate forecast OE, especially under positive-growth scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect capital expenditures for 2026 to increase compared with 2025 as we continue to expand globally and optimize our manufacturing and supply chain operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish that 2026 capital expenditures are expected to exceed 2025 and that first-half 2026 cash capital expenditures increased from $30.9m to $56.8m year over year. They do not quantify full-year spending or distinguish maintenance investment from discretionary expansion. The record therefore cannot establish the recurring OE adjustment or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2026 capital budget and asset-level maintenance-versus-growth classification, include developed software and capitalized cloud implementation costs, and rerun scenarios for any required reinvestment omitted from forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Cash added at par may carry unrecognized repatriation tax leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified tax leakage; the associated $127.2m indefinitely reinvested earnings balance is 2.5% of the $5,119m base equity value, and excluding that entire balance would reduce value by only $1.81 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any tax required to make foreign cash distributable would reduce the $534.9m cash bridge added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: No deferred tax liability has been recorded related to the repatriation of $ 127.2 million in earnings that are indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes the $127.2m earnings balance but neither connects it to the bridge cash nor quantifies a repatriation tax. Even the substantially more conservative assumption that the entire $127.2m is unavailable—not merely taxed—would reduce base value from $72.64 to about $70.83 per share and bull value from $84.34 to about $82.53, leaving both far below the $147.48 market price. The possible tax leakage therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map the $534.9m cash by jurisdiction and legal owner and estimate actual distribution taxes; adjust the bridge if desired, without reopening the valuation conclusion unless inaccessible balances exceed the disclosed $127.2m earnings amount.

audit_findings.title: The latest OE anchor depends heavily on a rapidly growing rebate estimate
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 U.S. pharmacy rebate provisions were $654.7m versus the $326.3m OE anchor, and accrued rebates were $205.5m at year-end 2025 and $259.7m at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated rebate provision would overstate net revenue, earnings, operating cash generation and the FY2025 OE anchor used throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: United States pharmacy rebate provisions charged against gross sales amounted to $654.7 million, $452.7 million, and $367.3 million in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The rebate estimate is demonstrably large and was identified by the auditor as a critical audit matter, but neither the provision's growth nor the subsequent reserve increase demonstrates an estimation error. No subsequent-payment or true-up evidence quantifies any shortfall. Materiality is therefore unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 provisions to 2026 payments and true-ups by payor and contract, test channel inventory and utilization assumptions, and rerun the anchor and scenarios for any identified provision deficiency.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling does not fully quantify maximum PSU dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: conservative upper bound of 310,275 incremental shares: 206,850 outstanding PSUs multiplied by the additional 150% needed to reach 250%; 0.44% of the 70.473199m denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental PSU vesting increases fully diluted shares and lowers value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain of these PSUs could ultimately vest at up to 250 % of the target award depending on the achievement of the performance and market criteria.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact maximum requires tranche-level terms, but treating every year-end PSU as target-based and eligible for 250% vesting produces a conservative incremental ceiling of 310,275 shares. That would reduce base value by approximately $0.32 per share and bull value by approximately $0.37, far too little to alter the conclusion relative to the $147.48 market price.
audit_findings.action: Calculate maximum vesting separately for each outstanding PSU tranche, subtract only demonstrably non-overlapping dilution buffers, and update the denominator if the resulting share count exceeds 70.473199m.

audit_findings.title: An expiring revenue stream is absent from the perimeter ruling
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 Drug Delivery revenue was $34.1m, 1.3% of $2,708.1m total revenue and 10.4% of the $326.3m OE anchor; first-half 2026 revenue fell to $9.1m from $25.1m
audit_findings.mechanism: Carrying Drug Delivery OE beyond the December 2028 agreement expiry would overstate forecast OE, growth and terminal value if the contract is neither renewed nor replaced.
audit_findings.evidence: Substantially all of our commercialized Drug Delivery revenue consists of sales of a customized version of our product for use in Amgen’s Neulasta Onpro kit under an agreement that expires in December 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The expiry is established and should be reflected explicitly, but the stream is small and already declining. As an intentionally conservative bound, treating the entire $34.1m of FY2025 revenue as recurring OE and removing it immediately would reduce bear, base and bull values to approximately $56.92, $65.84 and $76.33 per share, respectively. A phaseout after 2028 based on actual OE contribution would have a smaller effect and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $147.48 market price.
audit_findings.action: Isolate Drug Delivery revenue, direct costs, working capital and maintenance investment; phase its actual OE contribution out after 2028 unless renewal or replacement evidence supports continuation.
